items.headline: We asked, you answered: Labiotech’s 2026 reader survey results
items.preview: Labiotech surveyed its readers to understand their preferences and engagement.
items.article:
Labiotech conducted a survey among its newsletter subscribers to gather insights on their demographics, content preferences, and engagement levels. The results revealed that over 80% of respondents are senior decision-makers in the biotech industry, with a strong presence in Europe and North America.

Why this matters: The feedback highlights the importance of understanding audience needs in shaping content strategies. The survey results will guide Labiotech in enhancing its offerings, including new formats and improved user experience, to better serve its engaged readership.

items.headline: Will Capricor’s latest move give deramiocel new life?
items.preview: Capricor Therapeutics refocuses deramiocel's indication to improve limb function in DMD.
items.article:
Capricor Therapeutics announced a strategic shift in its Biologics License Application (BLA) for deramiocel, aiming to seek approval for improving limb function in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients. This change follows previous setbacks related to the drug's secondary endpoint in clinical trials.

Why this matters: The refocusing of the indication has positively impacted Capricor's stock, reflecting investor optimism about the potential for deramiocel to reach patients and address a critical need in DMD treatment.

items.headline: Levistilide A Drives Ferroptosis via RNF40-HSP90α Axis, Suppressing Colorectal Cancer Lung Metastasis
items.preview: Levistilide A shows promise in targeting colorectal cancer metastasis through ferroptosis.
items.article:
A study published in Cell Death Discovery reveals that levistilide A, a compound derived from a traditional medicinal plant, induces ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells, potentially suppressing lung metastasis. The research identifies the RNF40-HSP90α axis as a critical pathway in this process.

Why this matters: By targeting ferroptosis, a regulated form of cell death, levistilide A may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for treating metastatic colorectal cancer, which currently has limited effective options.

items.headline: Stable RNA elements open new possibilities for mRNA therapeutics
items.preview: Research identifies viral RNA elements that enhance mRNA stability and protein production.
items.article:
A team at the Institute for Basic Science has discovered compact viral RNA elements that can significantly enhance the stability of mRNA and increase protein production. This finding could lead to more effective mRNA-based therapeutics, including vaccines and cancer treatments.

Why this matters: By improving mRNA stability, these viral elements could reduce the amount of mRNA needed for therapeutic applications, potentially lowering side effects and broadening the scope of mRNA technologies.

items.headline: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals the emergence of medusa-specific cell states in the Aurelia coerulea scyphozoan
items.preview: Single-cell RNA sequencing provides insights into medusa-specific cell types in Aurelia coerulea.
items.article:
A study presents a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of Aurelia coerulea, revealing significant molecular changes during the transition from polyp to medusa. The research highlights the emergence of diverse cell types, including neural subtypes and striated muscles, and suggests evolutionary links to other cnidarians.

Why this matters: Understanding the molecular basis of cell type diversification in medusozoans can shed light on evolutionary processes and the development of complex body plans in the animal kingdom.
